h1: Electrical Panel Upgrades and Replacement in South Florida
intro: A failing panel shows it: breakers that trip repeatedly, a burning smell, scorch marks, or lights that dim when the AC starts. Sometimes the first sign is a letter from your insurer. We replace it once and handle the permit and inspector.

definition.heading: What an electrical panel upgrade is
definition.body: A panel upgrade removes your old load center and installs a modern one built to current code. Older panels wear out, run short on space, or use equipment insurers no longer accept. The result is safe, current, and insurable again.

symptoms.title: Your insurer or inspector flagged it
symptoms.body: A carrier notice or a 4-point inspection called out the panel. Coverage often will not renew until the equipment meets a modern standard.

symptoms.title: Breakers trip for no clear reason
symptoms.body: A breaker that will not hold is telling you something downstream is wrong, or that the breaker itself is worn out.

symptoms.title: You smell burning or see scorch marks
symptoms.body: Heat where there should be none. It usually points to a failing connection, and it deserves a look before it gets worse.

symptoms.title: You have a fuse box or a flagged brand
symptoms.body: An old fuse box, or a brand insurers flag like Zinsco or Federal Pacific. The name alone is often what an inspector reacts to.

localSections.heading: South Florida homes and the panels inside them
localSections.body: South Florida housing was built across many decades, and every era left its own electrical fingerprint. Heat, humidity, and salt air corrode the lugs and bus bars inside a panel, so equipment here ages faster than it would anywhere drier.

localSections.heading: Why carriers are driving so many upgrades
localSections.body: The Florida insurance market has tightened, and outdated electrical equipment is one of the first things carriers look at. An obsolete panel is a common reason the electrical section of a 4-point fails. Replace it, pass inspection, and the objection goes away.

guide.title: The complete guide to upgrading your electrical panel in South Florida

sections.heading: What a panel upgrade actually is
sections.body: Your panel is where utility power enters and divides into the circuits feeding your property. Breaker box, load center, fuse box, same thing. An upgrade replaces the old equipment, breakers, and grounding with a modern assembly built to current code and sized for how you actually use power.

sections.heading: The panels insurers flag: Zinsco, Federal Pacific, and old fuse boxes
sections.body: Zinsco and Federal Pacific panels, often labeled Stab-Lok, are obsolete brands whose breakers can fail to trip under a fault. Old fuse boxes are the other common flag. Genuine parts are hard to source, so replacement is the honest answer, and a modern panel removes the objection.

sections.heading: How to choose the right contractor
sections.body: Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor and South Florida Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record. Our in-house crew handles the replacement in one visit, pulls the permit, and meets the inspector. If your panel is safe and current, we will say so and leave it alone.

faqs.question: My insurance company flagged my panel. What now?
faqs.answer: Send us the notice or the 4-point report. In most cases the fix is a modern panel that passes inspection. We assess in person, pull the permit, and meet the inspector so the objection goes away.

faqs.question: I have a Zinsco or Federal Pacific panel. Do I have to replace it?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes. Both are obsolete brands with a documented history of breakers that can fail to trip, and parts are hard to source. If your panel is a safe, current brand, we will not talk you into replacing it.

faqs.question: Do I really need a permit for this?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you want one. It puts a licensed contractor and a county inspector between you and a costly mistake. We pull it, schedule the inspection, and meet the inspector on site.

faqs.question: Will my power be off during the work?
faqs.answer: For part of the day, yes. We tell you ahead of time what to expect so you can plan around it. Our in-house crew does this constantly, so it is a focused, one-visit job.
